patients.label: Case 1: 6-year-old girl with a left cheek nodule diagnosed as primary cutaneous CD4+ SMPLPD

identity_evidence.quote: We report a case of SMPLPD presenting as a facial nodule in a 6-year-old Saudi girl.
A 6-year-old Saudi girl presented to our dermatology clinic at King Fahad Specialist Hospital in Dammam with a 3-month history of an erythematous nodule on the left cheek.

attribution_limitations: Table 1 lists published SMPLPD cases from other authors, including a 6-year-old with a left cheek nodule; those rows are literature data, not this patient.
The 6-month follow-up is stated as "within a 6-month follow-up period" in the case text but "at 6-month follow-up" in the abstract and conclusion.
The text says medium-to-large-sized atypical T cells expressed PD-1, while the infiltrate is otherwise described as small-to-intermediate-sized and the caption says the tumor cells are PD-1 positive.

The source calls SMPLPD a definite type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma but also says its malignant potential is unknown and that it was reclassified as a lymphoproliferative disorder rather than a lymphoma.
"Saudi" is a nationality descriptor; the schema has no nationality attribute and the runtime prompt does not derive ethnicity from nationality.
